extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH K99/R00 (Pathway to Independence) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a K99/R00 (NIH Pathway to Independence) career development and research grant application, including research strategy, career development plan, institutional commitment, resource sharing, and authentication plans. Focused on meeting NIH/PHS-398 and SF424 form requirements for a postdoctoral-to-independent transition award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise summary of the project that presents background, significance, preliminary findings, hypotheses, specific aims, approaches, and expected impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text shows a compact narrative: describing the cytoskeleton as structural + functional, noting gaps in evidence, summarizing preliminary systems (LifeAct-mRuby live-cell imaging), outlining multi-pronged screens (live imaging, synthetic lethality, transcriptome, CRISPR-Cas9) and identifying key biological nodes. Should convey foundation for proposed work and overall goals (e.g., develop tools, identify regulators, assess physiological consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A short statement summarizing the relevance of the proposed research to public health or the mission of the funding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a required PHS/SF424 component (listed in Table of Contents). Though specific text not reproduced, include a succinct, lay-accessible explanation of project significance consistent with NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly stated hypotheses and discrete, testable aims (e.g., Aim 1.1, Aim 1.2, Aim 2) that define the objectives of the research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example aims state hypotheses (e.g., existence of a chromatin state promoting cytoskeletal health; tissue-specific and cell non-autonomous effects) and concrete questions to be answered (e.g., is overexpression in one tissue sufficient to preserve lifespan?). Aims should be focused, feasible, and linked to methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A rigorous multipronged plan describing experimental approaches, methods, preliminary data, and how each aim will be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample strategy includes in vivo live-cell imaging, synthetic lethality screens, transcriptome and whole-genome CRISPR screens, biochemical approaches (proximity labeling), and development of single-cell biochemical assays. Provide rationale for methods, integration of datasets, and anticipated outcomes; demonstrate feasibility with preliminary results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the candidate's background, training needs, career objectives, and concrete plans for professional development toward independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document should show how the K99 phase will complete postdoctoral training and enable transition to independent R00 phase; include planned mentorship, teaching/training opportunities, expected percent effort (example: 'Ryo will dedicate 100% of his time for research'), and target career outcomes (tenure-track faculty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A plan describing how the candidate will receive formal and informal training in responsible conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a required component (Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research). Provide specifics on coursework, mentoring, and institutional RCR activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signed/explicit commitments from the mentor(s) detailing the training, mentorship, resources, and oversight they will provide to the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mentor roles, mentoring plans, frequency of meetings, mentor's track record, and how mentorship will support the candidate's transition to independence (example letters and statements are present in the application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters documenting collaborators' commitments of effort, resources, and specific roles in the project and candidate's training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and include letters for co-sponsors, core facilities, and collaborators who will provide expertise or resources (Table of Contents includes 'Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants').

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal letter/statement from the institution/department confirming appointment, protected research time, available resources, and commitment to the candidate's career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: department letter confirming full-time appointment throughout K99 postdoctoral phase, continuation of salary not contingent on award, and 100% research time. Include description of institutional support (space, access to facilities, opportunities to teach/attend seminars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Institutional Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the institutional setting, departmental strengths, nearby laboratories, core facilities, and collaborative environment that will support the project and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample content enumerates neighboring labs (Tijan, Schekman, etc.), shared instrumentation, machine/electronic shops, media center, imaging core, sequencing and proteomics cores, and opportunities for seminars, retreats, and trainee interactions. Emphasize access to expertise and resources that directly enable the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources (laboratory, clinical, animal, computer, office, environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description of physical and institutional resources available to carry out the proposed research, including lab space, specialized rooms, computing, and collaborative infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lab square footage and capacity (e.g., 'main laboratory is approximately 2000 sq. ft.'), microscope rooms, tissue culture room, media center, shared cold/warm rooms, computer servers, storage (173 TB), network speeds (1.5 GB/sec read), VPN access, and access to institutional cores. Document how these meet the project's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment availability and imaging/sequencing cores
rubrics_metrics.description: List of major equipment and core instruments available to perform proposed experiments (microscopes, confocals, centrifuges, mass-spec, sequencing platforms, specialized sorters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample inventory includes Zeiss AxioObserver.Z1, Leica SP8 confocal, diSPIM light-sheet, PerkinElmer spinning disk, COPAS Biosort, Seahorse XFe96 Analyzer, Optima XP ultracentrifuge, qPCR machines, PRISM licenses, file servers, and access to proteomics and genomics core facilities. Indicate licensing/software availability (e.g., Huygens Deconvolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide total federal funds requested, per-year direct costs, and narrative justification linking budget items to the proposed research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SF424 items and Research & Related Budget sections are included in Table of Contents. Example budget totals shown (Total Federal Funds Requested: $990,540) and per-year subtotals listed; include justification for personnel, equipment, travel, sequencing, core services, and data sharing travel plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate whether human subjects are involved; if so, specify exemptions, IRB status, approvals, and Human Subject Assurance Number; answer required SF424/PHS questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SF424 'Are Human Subjects Involved?' checkbox appears (example shows 'No'). If 'Yes', include exemption numbers or IRB approval dates and documentation per PHS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals Use and IACUC Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used, specify IACUC review status, approval dates, and Animal Welfare Assurance Number as required by PHS forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SF424 'Are Vertebrate Animals Used?' checkbox appears (example shows 'No'). If 'Yes', provide IACUC details and compliance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan and Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for dissemination of data and research resources: how and where raw and processed data, reagents, and organisms will be shared with the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample commitments: publish raw and processed data with publications; deposit raw sequencing data in NCBI's GEO per NCBI guidelines; processed datasets provided through the journal; present unpublished data at conferences; fund travel to present at least two conferences per year; ensure public access per NIH standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing Model Organisms and Reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to deposit unique organisms and reagents in community repositories to ensure access (e.g., C. elegans strains, plasmids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample commitments: deposit all C. elegans strains to the C. elegans Genetics Center (CGC) and plasmids/expression vectors to Addgene; use streamlined MTAs; avoid restrictive MTAs that prevent subsequent access; note Bayh-Dole implications and institutional licensing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: Nematode strain validation and backcrossing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for validating genetic identity and integrity of C. elegans strains used/generated in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All strains synthesized/received/ordered will be validated using conventional single-worm genotyping; strains generated via mutagenesis/integration/CRISPR-Cas9 will be backcrossed to the N2 wild-type strain at least 8 times to eliminate background mutations and off-target effects; deposit strains to CGC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: Preventing genetic drift and maintenance schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to minimize and monitor genetic drift in maintained nematode strains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include maintaining strains at 15°C with ample food, in darkness, avoiding starvation; maintain animals for a maximum of 3 months for sick phenotypes and 6 months for otherwise healthy animals; re-thaw regularly from -80°C backups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: Nematode media component documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and control key media components that can affect experimental outcomes and report any media-specific effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application notes that peptone types and agar brands affect readouts, and age of plates and IPTG induction methods affect RNAi efficacy; for key experiments, effects across media components have been tested and any media-specific results will be documented and reported at publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: Antibody validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to validate specificity and performance of antibodies used in assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key antibodies (e.g., against actin, fluorescent proteins) will be validated by Western blot, immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, or flow cytometry using RNAi knockdown of target protein or competitive recombinant peptide against the epitope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: Chemical validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation of purchased chemicals to ensure suitability for proposed experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchased chemicals will be validated by analyses against published physiological phenotypes; no custom-synthesized chemicals are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: Tissue-specific promoter cross-validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify expression patterns and function of tissue-specific promoters by cross-checking multiple promoters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible, use multiple tissue-specific promoters and cross-validate results (example: neuronal expression cross-compare unc-119, rab-3, and rgef-1). Use previously validated promoters where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property, Licensing, and MTAs (Bayh-Dole compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional approach to IP arising from NIH-funded work, licensing practices, and commitments to make research materials available for non-commercial research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UC Berkeley reserves rights under Bayh-Dole; typically licenses research resources non-exclusively for commercial purposes unless overriding reasons exist; retains rights to provide materials to the research community even in exclusive licenses; uses central repositories (Jackson Laboratory, ATCC) when in-house maintenance is not feasible; intends to avoid entering into MTAs that include terms preventing subsequent access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data presentation and dissemination expectations (conferences and publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans and expectations for presenting and publishing results to ensure dissemination and compliance with NIH public access and data-sharing policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: present at least two conferences per year (Keystone, CSHL, Gordon meetings); results planned for peer-reviewed journals that allow public access per NIH standards; provide unrestricted access to all raw and processed datasets at publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF424/PHS Administrative Compliance (certifications, dates, signatures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete required administrative forms and certifications (SF424 R&R, PHS forms), include project start/end dates, applicant and institutional identifiers, and authorized representative signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example entries: project start and end dates (04/01/2020–03/31/2025), total federal funds requested fields, certifications and assurances statement ('By signing this application, I certify ...'), and authorized representative signature with date.
